marks.gloss_en: וכן הוא אומר: ובניהו בן יהוידע על הכרתי ועל הפלתי -- the Kereti and Peleti being the Sanhedrin
the verse: 'and Benayahu ben Yehoyada was over the Kereti and the Peleti' (II Sam 20:23)
מאי קרא? עורה כבודי עורה הנבל וכנור אעירה שחר -- the harp and lyre have woken [me], and I will now be awake until dawn
the verse: 'awake, my glory; awake, harp and lyre; I will awaken the dawn' (Ps 57:9)
דאמר מר: למד לשונך לומר איני יודע, שמא תתבדה ותאחז -- Moshe hedged as the maxim counsels
וכיון דמשה הוה ידע, למה ליה למימר כחצות?
משה קסבר: שמא יטעו אצטגניני פרעה ויאמרו משה בדאי הוא -- דאמר מר: למד לשונך לומר איני יודע
Moshe reasoned: lest Pharaoh's astrologers err [about the moment] and say 'Moshe is a liar' -- so he said 'about midnight'
משה לעולם הוה ידע, ודוד נמי הוה ידע -- the premise is denied: both knew
David knew exactly when midnight was (R' Zeira, 4a.4)
Moshe spoke at midnight of the 13th: 'tomorrow, at [a moment] like midnight now' -- כחצות is a comparison, so no uncertainty was ever expressed
Rav Ashi: Moshe stood at midnight of the 13th going into the 14th, and said: tomorrow, at [a moment] like midnight now, I go out -- כחצות is a comparison, not an approximation
וכיון דדוד הוה ידע, כנור למה ליה?
לאתעורי משנתיה -- to wake him from his sleep
the lyre was there to wake him from his sleep (not to tell him the hour)
Benayahu ben Yehoyada in the verse stands for the Sanhedrin
the Sages: the evening Shema may be recited until midnight (the cited mishnah clause)
מאי קרא -- ואדברה בעדתיך נגד מלכים ולא אבוש: David speaks of Torah before kings and is not ashamed
the verse for account 2: 'and I will speak of Your testimonies before kings and will not be ashamed' (Ps 119:46)
כדרבי יעקב בר אידי -- as Jacob, promised protection, still feared lest sin cause its forfeit, so David
R' Yaakov bar Idi set 'I am with you and will guard you' (Gen 28:15) against 'and Jacob feared greatly' (Gen 32:8) and resolved: Jacob said, lest sin cause [forfeit of the promise]
כדתניא: עד יעבר עמך ה' עד יעבר עם זו קנית -- two entries; Israel deserved a miracle in Ezra's days too, אלא שגרם החטא
ודוד מי קרי לנפשיה חסיד? והכתיב לולא האמנתי... ותנא משמיה דרבי יוסי -- David himself did not know whether he had a portion among the righteous; how then could he call himself pious?
the tanna in R' Yosei's name: the dots on לולא (Ps 27:13) teach that David said: I am sure You reward the righteous in the world to come, but I do not know whether I have a portion among them
שמא יגרום החטא -- his doubt was that a future sin might forfeit his portion, not doubt of his piety (= p_shema_yigrom_david)
the answer: David's doubt about his portion was not doubt of his piety -- he feared lest sin cause [forfeit of it]
David calls himself pious: 'keep my soul, for I am pious' (Ps 86:2)
account 2, first ground: while the kings sit in their honoured groups, David's hands are soiled with blood, foetus and afterbirth to purify a woman for her husband
his name was not Mefiboshet but Ish Boshet
R' Yochanan: his name was not Kilav but Daniel
of Kilav Solomon said 'my son, if your heart is wise, my heart will be glad, even mine' (Prov 23:15) and 'be wise, my son, and make my heart glad, that I may answer him who taunts me' (Prov 27:11)
'until Your people cross, Lord' (Ex 15:16) is the first entry into the Land
